items.stem: Gemini Code Assist generates a shell command to delete resources. What is the safest next step?

options.text: Review the command and confirm it against official docs before running
options.rationale: Correct: generated commands must be verified before any destructive action.

options.text: Run it immediately to save time
options.rationale: Running an unreviewed destructive command risks data loss.

options.text: Assume it is correct because it cites a doc
options.rationale: Citations can be wrong; verification is still required.

options.text: Grant the model owner permissions so it can run itself
options.rationale: Over-granting IAM to an assistant is unsafe and unnecessary.

items.explanation: Correct: verify generated commands, especially destructive ones, before running.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices when prompting Gemini for Google Cloud? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Provide specific context and constraints in the prompt
options.rationale: Correct: context and constraints produce more useful, scoped output.

options.text: Keep secrets and regulated data out of prompts
options.rationale: Correct: sensitive data should not be placed in prompts.

options.text: Paste production credentials so the model can act directly
options.rationale: Credentials must never be shared in prompts.

options.text: Accept the first answer without iterating
options.rationale: Iterating and refining usually improves the result.

items.explanation: Correct: specific context and keeping sensitive data out are both sound prompting practices.

items.stem: Which surface is designed to help you write and explain code inside your IDE?

options.rationale: Correct: Code Assist is the coding surface in the IDE and Cloud Shell.
The BigQuery console is for queries, not IDE coding assistance.
Billing reports show cost, not code help.
The Storage browser manages objects, not code.

items.explanation: Correct: Gemini Code Assist is the IDE and Cloud Shell coding surface.
